title: Former James Bond reacts to Robert Pattinson casting as 007
text:

 Brendan Morrow, USA TODAY Updated Tue, 17 November 2026 at 4:57 pm UTC 3 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. Robert Pattinson already has the 007 seal of approval.
 After the "Twilight" star, 40, was cast as James Bond , the oldest living former Bond actor shared his reaction on social media. George Lazenby , who starred as Bond in 1969's "On Her Majesty's Secret Service," posted a video message addressed to Pattinson on his Instagram account Monday, Nov. 16.
 "Robert, welcome to the most exclusive club in the world," he said in the clip. "But remember to enjoy yourself. Let's see if you have a 'this never happened to the other fella' moment. All the best, mate."
 Amazon MGM Studios announces on Nov. 16, 2026, that Robert Pattinson will be the new James Bond on the big screen. Lazenby, 87, took over as Bond after Sean Connery played the famed British secret agent in five consecutive films from 1962 to 1967. But "On Her Majesty's Secret Service" was Lazenby's first and only Bond movie: The next film, "Diamonds Are Forever," brought back Connery in the role. Roger Moore then took over in "Live and Let Die."
 Lazenby did not have any previous screen credits before he played Bond. In a previous interview with Jeremy Clarkson , he said his agent convinced him to walk away from the role after only one movie.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "It was very easy for the people who were advising me to tell me that James Bond was Sean Connery's thing, and it's over. And I bought it," he said, noting that although the plan was for him to play Bond in seven films, he never signed a contract.
 Pattinson was unveiled as the next Bond on Nov. 16: He'll debut in the role in an upcoming film by "Dune" director Denis Villeneuve, which does not have a release date or title set. The "Primetime" actor will be the eighth man to play the role, including David Niven's unofficial portrayal in the 1967 spoof "Casino Royale."

To start, here's Pattinson posing on the red carpet upon arriving at the world premiere of "The Odyssey" in London on July 6, 2026. (CARLOS JASSO, AFP via Getty Images) "James Bond is one of the most legendary characters in cinema, and to be entrusted with 007 is the honour of a lifetime," Pattinson said in a statement, adding that "to say this role is a dream come true is an understatement."
 None of the other former Bond actors have reacted to the news yet, though Pierce Brosnan weighed in while the casting search was underway. Speaking with Vanity Fair in early November, Brosnan said all of the stars who were reported to be in the running for Bond "are actors I admire," and he particularly endorsed Callum Turner , his former costar in "The Only Living Boy in New York." At the time, it was not known that Pattinson was also in the mix.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Late Bond star Roger Moore's son Geoffrey also expressed approval of the pick, telling The Daily Mail , "I think he'll make a fine Bond. He has the experience and hits the right demographic and he is British of course."
 George Lazenby attends the Leigh Steinberg Super Bowl Party at Sony Pictures Studios on Feb. 12, 2022, in Culver City, California. Meanwhile, Brad Pitt shared his reaction to the casting with Extra at the premiere of "The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth." Pitt, after hearing the news for the first time, approved. "I love this idea," he said, continuing, "Good call. I like it!" The Oscar winner also said he'd love to play a Bond villain. "I'd like to do that," he told Extra.
 Florence Pugh , who worked with both Pattinson and Villeneuve on the upcoming " Dune: Part Three ," has similarly expressed interest in a villain role. Speaking at the Elle Women in Hollywood event on Nov. 16, Pugh revealed she texted Villeneuve earlier that morning to say, "Congratulations on finding your Bond. Nice catch. Any villains with the size of 5-foot-4, female?"
